requirements.lead_text: Discuss with your counselor what citizenship in the community means and what it takes to be a good citizen in your community. Discuss the rights, duties, and obligations of citizenship, and explain how you can demonstrate good citizenship in your community, Scouting unit, place of worship, or school.

pamphlet_excerpts: Public Policy Includes: Public policy includes the goals the government sets as well as theactions required to achieve those goals.
Citizens Notvote Voluntarily: Some citizens do notvote, voluntarily giving up their voice in the government.
Othercitizens Not Care: Othercitizens do not know or care about what is going on in theircommunity, until a prison is built in their neighborhood, orthe crime rate grows.
They Upset Particularissue: Unless they are upset about a particularissue, most citizens leave the decisions to elected representatives and local activists.
step_by_step_procedure: People Feel Connected: People who feel connected to their community tend toparticipate.
Active Citizens Their: The more active citizens are in their community, withties to a school, youth groups, businesses, and service clubs, the more interest they.
Thatis Longtime Residents: Thatis why longtime residents often hold local offices.
Chance Now Build: You have a chance now to build connections in yourown community.

requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Using an electronic mapping tool or paper map, locate and pinpoint the following services and landmarks in your community. Determine and record the distances from your home including driving time AND either walking or biking time. (1) Chief government buildings such as your city hall, county courthouse, and public works/services facilities (2) Fire station, police station, and hospital nearest your home (3) Parks, playgrounds, recreation areas, and trails (4) Historical or other interesting points of interest (b) Chart the organization of your local or state government. Show the top offices and tell whether they are elected or appointed.

pamphlet_excerpts: Organization Typical County: Organization of one typical county government Municipalities A charter is aformal, legaldocument thatdefines theboundaries of acity.
Municipalities Cities Towns: Municipalities (cities, towns, villages, and boroughs) aredensely populated urban areas with local governments.
Thestate Creates Them: Thestate creates them by charters or other legislation, which thenserve as local constitutions.
Municipal Governments: Municipal governments are organized according to theircharters.
step_by_step_procedure: Widely Form City: The most widely used form of city government is themayor-council charter.
Voters Elect Mayor: Voters elect a mayor as the chief executive and a council as its legislature.
Cities Larger Than: For cities larger than 5,000 people, the average size of a city council is seven members, buthuge cities like New York City may have as many.
Depending Formal Powers: Depending on how many formal powers are givento the mayor, the mayor-council form of government often isdescribed as a “strong-mayor”.

pamphlet_excerpts: Editorial Apiece Writingthat: An editorial is apiece of writingthat expresses thewriter’s opinions.
Editorials Usuallyare: Editorials usuallyare separatedfrom regularnews stories inthe newspaper.
Learn Lot Community: You can learn a lot about your community just by payingattention to what is going on around you.
Hearpeople Talking Grocery: You might hearpeople talking in the grocery store, in the post office, inrestaurants, or in the stands at athletic events.
step_by_step_procedure: Listen Closely Read: Listen closely, read the newspaper, watch the local news on television, andyou will find out what issues concern the public.
Hear Caraccidents Occurred: Or you might hear that many caraccidents have occurred at a particular intersection.
Mightsee News Coverage: You mightsee news coverage on television about how graffiti has been aproblem in a particular community.
Haveattended Court Session: If you haveattended a court session, you might have discovered connections between cases in the courtroom and articles in thepaper.

step_by_step_procedure: Out Sidesof Issue: Try to find out as much as you can about all sidesof the issue.
Citizens Older Eligible: Citizens 18 or older usually are eligible to run forlocal office.

pamphlet_excerpts: Quick Overview Variety: For a quick overview of the variety of services provided by yourcommunity, look under “Government and Community Services” (the blue pages) in your.
Search Theinternet Parent: Or, search theinternet with your parent or guardian’s permission.
Municipal Courts Citywide: Municipal courts have citywide authority and are organizedin divisions: civil, criminal, domestic relations, small claims, traffic, and probate.
Sit Session Oneof: If you sit in on a session of oneof these courts, you will hear cases involving misdemeanors (less serious crimes) and matters involving small amounts.
step_by_step_procedure: County State Courts: County and state courts (known as general trial courts) handle more serious civil and criminal cases, which are triedbefore a judge.
Instances Case Appealed: In some instances, a case is appealed to the state’s Supreme Court, which is the court of last resort in the state’sjudicial system.
Seven Justices Sit: Five to seven justices sit on the high benchand have the final say about all cases relating to state law.
Onrare Occasions Question: Onrare occasions, when a question of federal law is involved, acase may be appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court.

pamphlet_excerpts: Citizen Looks Opportunities: A good citizen looks for opportunities to help improve the community.
Small Efforts Difference: Small efforts make a difference, and you also can joinforces with others to benefit many people.
Young Citizens Participate: Young citizens who participate in Scouting, school activities, and religiousorganizations tend to volunteer far more often than students.
Willingness Continues: This willingness to help continues into adulthood.
step_by_step_procedure: Fulfilling Requirement Real: By fulfilling requirement 7, you will make a real contribution to yourcommunity and open the door to a lifetime of rewarding experiences.
Enjoy Doing Something: You know how much more you enjoy doing something if youare good at it or if it really interests you.
Mindas Consider Volunteer: So keep that in mindas you consider volunteer opportunities.
Think Willing Teach: Think about whether you are willing to teach thoseskills to other people.

Commonly Tracked: Commonly tracked characteristics include ethnicity, age, income, religious preference, and level of education.
Community Enthusiastic: Every community needs an enthusiastic supporter who willpromote it as a great place to live.
Booster Foryour Community: You can be a booster foryour community when you make your public presentation forrequirement 8.

Include Something Community: Include something about your community’s geography.
